subject.title: Albany — Measure T (Street Trees & Streetlighting Parcel Tax Measure)

text: Shall the measure to enact a special parcel tax on non-exempt property in the City at $0.0354 per lot square foot to maintain and improve public street trees and streetlighting to enhance local safety and sustainability, subject to an annual consumer price index adjustment up to 3%, exempting qualifying low-income residents, providing an estimated $775,000 annually until ended by voters, be adopted?
A “yes” vote on Measure “T” will approve this street trees and streetlighting improvement and maintenance parcel tax.
A “no” vote on Measure “T” will not approve this street trees and streetlighting improvement and maintenance parcel tax.

On July 6, 2026, the City Council voted to place Measure “T” on the November 3, 2026 General Municipal Election ballot. If approved by two-thirds (2/3) of Albany voters, this Measure would enact a new special parcel tax on property within the City to fund street trees and streetlighting improvements and maintenance as follows:
Establish a rate at $0.0354 per taxable lot square foot commencing July 1, 2027, subject to an annual Consumer Price Index (CPI) adjustment and an annual 3% cap;
Provide that only the first 500,000 lot square feet of a parcel would be subject to the tax and any square footage above 500,000 on a parcel would be exempt from the tax;
Establish a 100% exemption for residential parcels owned by qualifying very low-income residents, and a 50% exemption for qualifying low-income resident owners, as defined therein; and

Establish a 100% rebate to qualifying very low-income renters of tax imposed on a rental unit where they reside, and a 50% rebate to similarly qualifying low-income renters, as defined therein.
This tax would apply to possessory interests (i.e. leaseholds) on a parcel where the owner is exempt from parcel taxation. The tax is estimated to generate $775,000 annually until repealed by voters at a subsequent election. The revenue from this tax would be deposited into a dedicated “Street Trees and Streetlighting Special Tax Fund” and used for “Street Trees Improvement and Maintenance” and “Streetlighting Improvement and Maintenance”, as those terms are defined in the Measure. This parcel tax would be collected the same and be subject to the same requirements as other property taxes collected by the County of Alameda on behalf of the City of Albany.
This Measure would require the City’s Finance Director to prepare an annual accountability report showing: (i) parcel tax revenues collected and spent; and (ii) status of projects/work funded with tax revenues.

be mailed at no cost to you.
Vote YES on Measure T to keep Albany safe, green,

text:
Every day, we rely on streetlights and street trees. Streetlights help people walking, rolling, biking, and driving see one another at night for safe travel, especially at busy intersections. Trees shade our sidewalks, clean our air, cool our streets, absorb stormwater, and make Albany’s neighborhoods more beautiful.
But Albany’s streetlighting and street trees need dedicated, reliable funding. The lamps installed decades ago are failing and the City’s Streetlighting Evaluation identified many intersections that need more lighting. Reliable funding would also help close the lighting gaps residents see every day on neighborhood streets.
For street trees, their maintenance is the responsibility of the adjacent property owner. To the extent the City provides maintenance, it only has funding to react once a tree has developed a substantial problem. Many parts of the City have too few street trees at all. The City’s Street Tree Management Plan recommends the City provide proactive maintenance to improve the health and plant more trees to increase the extent of our urban forest.
The City does not have funding to meet these needs. Measure T creates a fair property tax whose revenue is dedicated to street lighting and street tree maintenance and improvements. The average cost per house is $12/month and per condominium $3/month. Households with very low-income get full relief from the tax and those with low income get 50% relief.
A
vote means safer streets and sidewalks through better lighting and a more resilient, sustainable, and beautiful Albany through healthier and more trees.

strong: Protect what makes Albany livable, walkable, and
welcoming. Vote YES on Measure T.
